name: Edward Hovell-Thurlow, Lord Thurlow
bio: Edward Hovell-Thurlow, 2nd Baron Thurlow (1781–1829), was an English poet and nephew of the Lord Chancellor of the same title. He published several volumes of verse in the 1810s and 1820s.
His lyric "May" is printed in The Oxford Book of English Verse.

poems.title: May
poems.author: Edward Hovell-Thurlow, Lord Thurlow
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of English Verse (1900)
poems.text:
May! queen of blossoms,
  And fulfilling flowers,
With what pretty music
  Shall we charm the hours?
Wilt thou have pipe and reed,
Blown in the open mead?
Or to the lute give heed
  In the green bowers?

Thou hast no need of us,
  Or pipe or wire;
Thou hast the golden bee
  Ripen’d with fire;
And many thousand more
Songsters, that thee adore,
Filling earth’s grassy floor
  With new desire.

Thou hast thy mighty herds,
  Tame and free-livers;
Doubt not, thy music too
  In the deep rivers;
And the whole plumy flight
Warbling the day and night--
Up at the gates of light,
  See, the lark quivers!
